DRO ZERO — Setup P1 zero, mm, linear mode

DRO FIRST USE

Use ABS mode in mm. Coordinates describe the tool relative to the work; the table moves the opposite way. Axis Set assigns the current position's coordinate; Preset stores a destination and does not establish this datum.

For an opposed-edge datum, use the same finder for both actual edges:

  1. Pick up each actual edge and compensate its signed contact.
  2. Use their actual midpoint (edge 1 + edge 2) / 2; set the stated datum there, not at half an assumed stock width.
  3. Before a check jog, raise Z only until the tip clears the work and all clamps; return to the contact reading before lowering, without another Axis Set.

This setup's paper is 0.05 mm: stop at light drag and include that actual thickness with the contact-side sign in Axis Set.

From X -179.54, jog +X 10 mm: it must read -169.54; -189.54 means reversed — STOP and correct the direction before re-establishing the datum.

X and Y check jog
  1. raise Z only until the tool clears the work and clamps, without changing the axis under test.
  2. jog the table by the stated check-jog amount in the positive tool-relative direction; the display must read the listed value.
  3. jog back to the Axis Set value again, then lower; do not Axis Set again.

EDGE FINDER — 0.2 in edge finder

Tip Ø 5.08 mm; radius 2.54 mm.

Speed: 750–1500 rpm (finder 750–1500; mill 50–3000; use only the intersecting spindle ranges).

Mechanical contact: offset the tip while stopped; run at the stated speed. Approach in small handwheel steps until it runs true and kicks sideways; back off and repeat the first kick to locate the edge.

Offset: at the pick-up the spindle axis is half the tip Ø (5.08) off the edge, r = 2.54. Coming from the − side (moving + onto the edge): Axis Set edge − 2.54. Coming from the + side: Axis Set edge + 2.54. Each DRO ZERO row prints its signed Axis Set.

Finder data: Starrett 827A: mechanical edge finder, .200 in contact Ø, .375 in body, single end (starrett.com Edge & Center Finders listing); 750-1500 rpm for a .200 in mechanical edge finder; tip centres then breaks away at the edge (Travers Tool Co., How to Use a .200 in Edge Finder, solutions.travers.com, 2025).

T4C op 10 — profile outer · T1 1/4 in 4fl EM · Z -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5, -2.7 · conventional

6 depth levels, top first, at the Zs in the heading: run the whole path below at each. Get down at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 11.43; at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 9.43; at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 7.43; at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 5.43; at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 3.43; at the pass starting X 43.95, Y 3.175: plunge from the level above (level 1 from Z 0) at 35 mm/min; at every other pass start, clear of the stock: lower to the level's Z. Between levels, lift to Z 3 (above the stock), rapid back to pass 1.

Done: level 1 of 6 level 2 of 6 level 3 of 6 level 4 of 6 level 5 of 6 level 6 of 6

SETUP T4 — PM-30MV

DEMONSTRATION single-axis side milling of TAPER NEG; no oblique hand-saw clearing-box substitution.

Starts from: part as it arrives from Setup T4C — top at Z 0, bottom at Z -2.485.

HOLD

  1. Mount the Rocker central-seat clocked edge milling cradle (shop-made: SHOP-MADE FIXTURE table, Setup T4).
  2. Rocker central-seat clocked edge milling cradle: base flat on the table, underside at Z -28.4892 (Make-to-drawing placement).
  3. Support table-base: Designed table-fixed circular base for four rocker edge clockings (shop-made: SHOP-MADE FIXTURE table, Setup T4); local origin X -97.861, Y -89.755, Z -28.4892 mm; local +X toward +X; local +Z toward +Z. DEMONSTRATION independent table-aligned base: top seats at cradle local Z-26 after actual 10 mm base thickening; work seat and primary pose unchanged. Nominated example central T-slot attachment and recessed M6 fixture mounts; use matching clocking pattern, torque and verify seating before pickups. Not a vendor observation.
  4. Stop: With spindle isolated, clock the straight cradle base datum edge (fixture local Y-35) using DTI at fixture X-50 and +50. Move table between their transformed coordinates (100 mm times hold.pose.x), alternating single axes with safe retract; tap lightly until endpoint readings agree within 0.01 mm. Tighten recessed M6 mounts in matching base pattern, recheck both endpoints, then indicate socket centre. Hole pattern alone is not angle acceptance; target plane Y0, waste +Y.
  5. Two separately declared central press clamps over supported finished strap.
  6. Both tip scrap kits remain removed. No unsupported scrap clamp or lower-rail seat is carried through this taper cut.
  7. C1 clamp: Rocker separate central edge-milling press clamp (shop-made: SHOP-MADE FIXTURE table, Setup T4).
  8. C2 clamp: Rocker separate central edge-milling press clamp (shop-made: SHOP-MADE FIXTURE table, Setup T4).
  9. Note: Integral central support for finished strap; relieved base below breakthrough, cutter and offcut outside central cradle. DEMONSTRATION rotated cradle and part together. No CL/CR waste is used as the hold after end trimming; verify seating and re-indicate every rehold.

Coolant: cutting oil brush.

SETUP J1 — bench

Press completed MHA-CH-12 hub into completed MHA-CH-13 socket; no brazing/compound route.

Starts from: parts from Setup H1 and Setup T4 joined. Joined by press fit (clean/dry matched surfaces; use aligned press with annular support at the socket and stopped ram to leave supply stock at both hub ends. Press continuously and square, never hammer. No retaining compound is specified. STOP for excess force, cocking, scoring or strap distortion. Confirm actual land minus socket is 0.01016–0.03302 mm before pressing; neither measurement nor stock preparation may be inferred from nominal dimensions.): spigot hub land into through-socket strap socket, interference 0.01016 to 0.03302 mm diametral.
